question:
The Bohr model of the hydrogen atom treats the electron motion using non-relativistic mechanics.

For this question, use the following provided relations for hydrogen:

1) Ground-state speed: $v_1=\dfrac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\hbar}$.

2) Fine-structure constant: $\alpha=\dfrac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\hbar c}$ and $\alpha\approx\dfrac{1}{137}$.

Evaluate whether the non-relativistic assumption is justified by doing the following:

(i) Using the given definitions, derive the ratio $\dfrac{v_1}{c}$ in terms of $\alpha$ (core derivation).

(ii) Hence calculate the numerical value of $\dfrac{v_1}{c}$ and express it as a percentage (application/inference).

(iii) Based on your result, evaluate whether treating the motion as non-relativistic is reasonable for hydrogen ground state and justify your conclusion in one or two clear statements.

options.A: $\dfrac{v_1}{c}\approx \dfrac{1}{137}$; Yes, the speed is less than $1\%$ of $c$, so relativistic effects are negligible for hydrogen ground state.
options.B: $\dfrac{v_1}{c}\approx 0.5$; No, relativistic effects must be included.
options.C: $\dfrac{v_1}{c}\approx 1$; No, the electron moves at the speed of light.
options.D: $\dfrac{v_1}{c}\approx 0.1$; Yes, but large corrections are required already in the ground state.
